raw:
{
  "need": "Competence",
  "secondary": { "name": "Status" },
  "read": "This student's tears are not manipulation — they signal that mistakes feel like verdicts on their worth, not just their work. Softened feedback accidentally confirms their fear: that the real standard is too high for them, which is its own quiet wound to status.",
  "pull": { "collapse": "Protector", "instinct": "Watering down feedback to keep the peace feels kind in the moment, but it robs the student of accurate information and sends the message that you do not believe they can handle the truth — which is a hidden form of disrespect." },
  "mentorMove": "Separate the person from the draft: hold the full standard for the work while making it unmistakably clear you see a capable person on the other side of the red ink. Name the tears as normal and keep the feedback honest anyway.",
  "holdFirm": [
    "The standard for the work does not drop because the reaction is emotional.",
    "Every specific piece of feedback you were going to give still gets said — just anchored in belief, not just correction."
  ],
  "stayFlexible": [
    "Deliver the feedback in writing first so they can absorb it before talking, if that helps them regulate.",
    "Let them choose whether the debrief happens right now or after a short breather — same conversation, just timed differently."
  ],
  "forceLevel": { "level": 1, "label": "Empathy" },
  "script": [
    { "phase": "Connection", "words": "Hey — I noticed this kind of lands hard when I mark up your work, and I want to talk about that for a second before we dig in." },
    { "phase": "Curiosity", "words": "When you see the comments, what goes through your head first — is it more like frustration with the work, or does it feel more like something about you?" },
    { "phase": "Collaboration", "words": "Here is what I want you to know: the fact that I am giving you the full, honest picture is because I think you can actually use it. A lot of teachers pull their punches with students they are not sure about. I am not pulling mine with you. That is a compliment, even if it does not feel like one." },
    { "phase": "Commitment", "words": "So here is the deal going forward — I am going to keep telling you exactly what the work needs, and you are going to keep bringing it back. I have high standards for this, and I genuinely believe you can get there. Deal?" }
  ],
  "longGame": "Over time, reframe every revision cycle as evidence of growing capability — point to specific moves the student made from one draft to the next so they build a track record they can see, shifting their identity from someone who fears judgment to someone who uses it."
}
situation: A sensitive student tears up whenever I correct their work, and I find myself softening real feedback to avoid it.
